class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="docs: record the inline numeral and the verse-3 boundary

Two facts about digits that the symbol table got wrong or omitted.

It claimed digits appear only in the final sections. They do not: page 10 line 7
carries a black, rune-sized 7 set inline with a separator dot on each side, at
rune 2,566 inside the encrypted corpus. It is the only inline numeral there,
every other digit before rune 12,956 being part of a base-60 block or a verse
number. It is the precedent for treating a numeral as a word-level token, and it
yields no word of its own, since a word is a run of runes.

Verse 3 opens without a closing mark, and that is on the page. Four of the five
verses are closed by a cluster mark; verse 3 is preceded directly by the runes
FB with nothing between them and the numeral, which both the image and an
independent read of the scan confirm.

No marker is written there and none should be. A circled numeral would claim a
dot count the page does not show, and a '-' would show a separator it does not
have -- besides colliding with the base-60 spacing, which is what '-' records in
these files, never a rune-word boundary. The transcription keeps exactly what is
there. The boundary is carried by the numeral, which WORD_BOUNDARY honours, so
writing nothing loses nothing.

The choice moves one word out of 2,928, so no statistic turns on it. It is
recorded so FB is not later read as an ordinary short word." class="Link--secondary" href="/cicada-solvers/aldegonde/commit/00557c9e1e7b27556b05bdb02cdf48ec9ba4a742">docs: record the inline numeral class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="Resolve the lag-5 word-boundary contradiction

Two consolidated research lines disagreed about the same +32 lag-5
coincidence excess: one characterized it as match pairs at separations
{1,4} that 'freely cross word boundaries', the other as an excess that
'exists only inside words'. Neither ran the other's test.

Add the joint test both skipped: classify all 479 lag-5 matches by
(paired vs isolated) x (within-word vs across-word) and judge each cell
against a per-section word-length permutation null over the
byte-identical rune stream (experiments/lag5_word_boundary.py, which
also reproduces both published instruments exactly: 102/2073 within vs
377/10878 across, and 29/28 pair events vs ~17.7 expected).

Result: paired matches are word-boundary-aware (27 within vs null
16.9 +/- 4.1, p = 0.014) - boundary-blindness is falsified - and so are
isolated matches (75 vs 59.5 +/- 6.8, p = 0.018). Nine of the 29 d1
pair events are exactly the nine in-word XY...XY repeat words. The
pairing and the within-word excess are two faces of one word-aware
phenomenon: the count excess lives inside words, while the {1,4}
pairing extends across boundaries (a d4 event spans 10 positions and
cannot usually fit inside a word).

The core statistics are library code with unit tests:
aldegonde.analysis.coincidence gains word_index_map, recut_words,
boundary_coincidence, and boundary_permutation_test (including planted
word-aware and boundary-blind synthetic controls in the tests).

Update lag5-phenomenon.md, lag5-digraph-structure.md,
within-word-d5-coincidence.md, and the README constraint: the
mechanism sees the word structure." class="Link--secondary" href="/cicada-solvers/aldegonde/commit/dc62fb9a2b4e095d46cad3afb57eaa498610da5e">Resolve the lag-5 word-boundary The transcription records dot marks with two characters, `-` and `.`, which
collapses at least five distinct glyphs on the page (mark-glyph-inventory.md).
Replacing them with circled numerals carrying the dot count needs the code to
accept those characters first, so this lands ahead of any data change and works
with either encoding.

src/aldegonde/c3301.py gains the single source of truth:

    DOT_MARKS      ① … ㉟, circled by dot count
    LEGACY_MARKS   - .
    MARKS          both
    STRUCTURE      % & $
    WORD_BOUNDARY  MARKS | STRUCTURE
    LINE_WRAP      / and newline, which are NOT word boundaries

experiments/lp_corpus.py, the canonical loader, uses WORD_BOUNDARY, so the next
encoding change is one line there rather than forty files.

The remaining scripts have their boundary literals extended, "-.%&$" becoming
"①-.%&$". That is a superset, so no script's behaviour can drift: files in
either encoding parse identically. Four tokenised on a bare "-" and were read
individually rather than patched by regex -- anomaly_scan, gap_audit,
quote_span_analysis and lp.py.

Verified against the UNMIGRATED data, which is the point of landing this first:
283 tests pass and lp_corpus reports 12,956 runes / 2,928 words / 86 doublets,
unchanged. The corpus consumers reproduce their published numbers exactly --
two_rune_depth 465 words and 107,880 pairs, word_depth_by_length 112 observed
against 125.4 chance, quote_span_word_lengths 13.6% inside and 19.4% outside.

Also in this batch, from the review tooling built alongside:
 - apply_review enforces two hard limits rather than trusting them: no line is
   ever added or removed, and no rune is ever changed. Both abort without
   writing. Content the transcription omits -- the cuneiform on pages 33-39,
   the picture on page 2 -- is reported and left out, because adding it is a
   maintainer decision, not a side effect of a mark pass.
 - the review page reads the new encoding, and its generated script is

class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="feat: accept the circled-numeral mark encoding

The transcription records dot marks with two characters, `-` and `.`, which
collapses at least five distinct glyphs on the page (mark-glyph-inventory.md).
Replacing them with circled numerals carrying the dot count needs the code to
accept those characters first, so this lands ahead of any data change and works
with either encoding.

src/aldegonde/c3301.py gains the single source of truth:

    DOT_MARKS      ① … ㉟, circled by dot count
    LEGACY_MARKS   - .
    MARKS          both
    STRUCTURE      % & $
    WORD_BOUNDARY  MARKS | STRUCTURE
    LINE_WRAP      / and newline, which are NOT word boundaries

experiments/lp_corpus.py, the canonical loader, uses WORD_BOUNDARY, so the next
encoding change is one line there rather than forty files.

The remaining scripts have their boundary literals extended, "-.%&$" becoming
"①-.%&$". That is a superset, so no script's behaviour can drift: files in
either encoding parse identically. Four tokenised on a bare "-" and were read
